entities.summary:
Ausiàs March was a Valencian poet and knight from Gandia, Valencia, who played a crucial role in the development of the 'Golden Century' of Valencian literature. Born in 1400, he was a prominent figure in the court of King Martin I of Aragon and served as a knight in the service of the Crown of Aragon. March's poetry, which explored themes of love, nature, and the human condition, was widely acclaimed and helped to establish him as one of the leading poets of his time. His works, including the epic poem 'Cantigas de Sant Jordi,' are still studied and admired today for their beauty, depth, and historical significance.

Through his poetry, March helped to promote the use of the Valencian language and culture, which had been suppressed by the dominant Castilian language and culture of the time. His efforts contributed to the revitalization of Valencian identity and helped to pave the way for future generations of writers and artists. March's legacy extends beyond his own work, as he helped to establish the foundations for the development of modern Valencian literature.

March's influence can also be seen in the works of later writers, such as the 16th-century poet and historian, Lluc de Serrallach. His poetry and style have been praised for their beauty, clarity, and emotional depth, and continue to be studied and admired by scholars and readers today.

In conclusion, Ausiàs March was a significant figure in the development of Valencian literature, who played a crucial role in promoting the use of the Valencian language and culture, and helped to establish the foundations for the development of modern Valencian literature.

Ausiàs March's poetry is characterized by its use of the Valencian language, its exploration of themes such as love, nature, and the human condition, and its use of symbolism and imagery. His works are notable for their beauty, depth, and historical significance, and continue to be studied and admired by scholars and readers today.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ausiàs March was a poet and a knight who lived in the 15th century. He was born in Beniarjó, Valencia, and served the Crown of Aragon and the kingdom of Valencia. March's poetry helped to promote the use of the Valencian language and culture, which had been suppressed by the dominant Castilian language and culture of the time. His works contributed to the revitalization of Valencian identity and helped to pave the way for future generations of writers and artists.
